title: Sixteen Summers and One Locked Gate
subtitle: 愿望与追求 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 愿望与追求（做人与做事·愿望与追求）
meta: 主题语境：愿望与追求（做人与做事·愿望与追求）　|　核心词汇：desire　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 desire 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1947 my great-uncle ① held a desire that no neighbour in the lane would have understood, and he said the holding was the whole of the summer. The ② desire, meaning the longing and not the request, ran sixteen summers and stayed unspoken; a desire, he said, is the only thing in a heart that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ desire in that house had the same locked gate at the end of it, and the ④ desire at the end, meaning the one he kept for the orchard and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever granted twice. A desire, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to ask; my great-uncle said the asking is the part that fills sixteen summers.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the desire was the whole of the letter, meaning the request and not the longing. The ⑥ desire, meaning the request and not any of that, is the only thing in a letter that everybody reads and nobody grants; desire, she said, is either something you hold or the only word that means both a longing and a request. She said the request is the part they remember.

By 1956 the ⑦ desire had become a line in a will, and the will had become an argument about the locked gate. The ⑧ desire of the whole thing, my great-uncle wrote in July, was one house and sixteen summers of asking; desire, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to ask. She said the asking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ desire I remember is the one at the end, which was granted in 1970 and is still described as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ desire, my grandmother said in 1972, is the only thing that improves by being granted; every desire, she said, is a request that has agreed to look like a longing. She said the request was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 愿望；渴望（指一家人心里的那一份）
B. n. 渴望（指那份眷恋本身，与那个请求相对）
C. 固定搭配：hold a desire 怀有一份愿望
D. n. 愿望（指留给果园的那一份）
E. n. 愿望；心愿（抽象总称，指一屋子人的期盼）
F. n. 愿望（指遗嘱里写到、被列明的那一份）
G. n. 请求；要求（指信里提出的那一项）
H. n. 请求（抽象总称，指人人读到却无人允准的那一项）

items.q: held a desire that no neighbour in the lane would have understood
The desire, meaning the longing and not the request
the desire was the whole of the letter
the desire had become a line in a will
The desire of the whole thing
A desire, my grandmother said in 1972

answers.why: hold a desire 意为“怀有一份愿望”，1947 年伯祖父怀有一份巷子里没有一位邻居能理解的愿望。
desire 意为“渴望”，指那份眷恋本身而不是那个请求，它历经十六个夏天而始终没有说出口。
desire 意为“愿望、渴望”，指那栋房子里每一份愿望，每一份末尾都有同一扇锁着的门。
desire 意为“愿望”，指留给果园的那一份，是唯一有人允准过两次的。
desire 意为“请求、要求”，指信里提出的那一项，母亲说这项请求就是那封信的全部。
desire 意为“请求”，指人人读到却无人允准的那一项而不是那份眷恋，是信里人人都读到、却无人允准的东西。
desire 意为“愿望”，指遗嘱里写到、被列明的那一份，到 1956 年这份愿望成了遗嘱里的一行。
desire 意为“愿望、心愿”，伯祖父七月写道，整件事的心愿是一栋房子和十六个夏天的请求。
desire 意为“愿望”，我记得的是末尾那一份，1970 年被允准，至今仍被说成屋里最安静的一份。
desire 为抽象总称，祖母 1972 年说，一份愿望是唯一会因为被允准而变得更好的东西。
